introH2: 🏖️ How many kinds of Chao Lao Beach stays are there, and how do you pick the right one for your trip?
introHtml: Chao Lao Beach and the adjoining Laem Sadet Beach form a long stretch of coast in Tha Mai district, Chanthaburi, and they've become a go-to weekend drive for people from Bangkok and the eastern provinces — you can get there in a day, and the stays cost less than Hua Hin or Pattaya. But "a Chao Lao beachfront stay" doesn't have one single look — some are beachfront hotels with a private beach and a sea-view pool in the low-thousand-baht range, some are family resorts packed with a waterslide pool and kids' activities, and some are pool villas or quiet seaside houses where you can bring a pet. A lot of people book by the photos and then find the stay is "near the beach" but you have to cross a road, or the sea on this side is murkier than they expected, so it feels like it didn't match the pictures. This article gathers 10 Chao Lao–Laem Sadet beachfront stays that we've reviewed in depth — every one comes from reading guests' real reviews, covering the upsides and the honest caveats, comparing prices across 3 sites, with direct booking links throughout, so you can pick the one that genuinely fits your trip.
mrtHtml: Chao Lao Beach is in Tha Mai district, Chanthaburi, about 25–30 min by car from Chanthaburi town and roughly 3.5–4 hours from Bangkok via the motorway. There's no public transport that runs all the way to the beach, so having your own car or a rental is by far the easiest — if you take a coach to Chanthaburi town you'll need a connecting ride. The stays in this article sit in: Chao Lao Beach (Chaloem Burapha Chonlathit Road, Khlong Khut subdistrict) — the main, long beach, with stays lined up the whole way, swimmable, with seafood restaurants and an evening market; and Laem Sadet Beach — south of Chao Lao, quieter, with a nicer beach in places. Nearby is the Kung Krabaen Bay mangrove nature study centre, the area's signature day trip, about 10–15 min by car from most of the stays.

entries.type: 3-Star Beachfront Hotel · On Chao Lao Beach
entries.name: Chaolao Tosang Beach Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Chao Lao Beach · beachfront, private beach
entries.addr: 44/4 Moo 5, Chaloem Burapha Chonlathit Road, Khlong Khut subdistrict, Chao Lao Beach, Tha Mai
entries.storyHtml: If we start with the stay people on Chao Lao Beach talk about most, plenty of reviews put Chaolao Tosang Beach Hotel first — an 86-room, 3-star beachfront hotel that genuinely sits right on Chao Lao Beach, with a private beach you can walk down to swim from, and the largest stack of reviews in this article: over 1,145, scoring about 8.6 on Trip.com, which reflects how long it's been open and the steady stream of guests. What brings people back is a starting price that's very light for sleeping right by the sea — Superior rooms start around ฿1,800, while anyone after a full sea view can step up to a Beachfront room facing straight out to the water. The thing reviews agree on most is the sea-view pool and a separate kids' pool, which let families with little ones splash around all day without going into the sea itself, plus staff that many call friendly and genuinely helpful. Breakfast is a buffet that most reviews call decent for the price — nothing flashy, but filling. Honest caveats from the reviews: it's a hotel that's been open a long while, so rooms in the older block look their age and some smell musty, so ask for the newer block or a recently renovated room. The sea on the Chao Lao side is sand mixed with mud and not as clear as island water, and the public beach beyond the hotel's stretch has litter in places during the monsoon season. This isn't a luxury hotel, but it's the best value per baht for a family driving down to splash around on Chao Lao Beach without overthinking it.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: ask for a room in the newer block or a recently renovated one, and avoid the older block that reviews say smells musty. If the sea view matters to you, pick a Beachfront or Deluxe Sea View room outright, since Superior rooms mainly face the garden or inward.

entries.type: 4-Star Beachfront Resort · On Chao Lao Beach
entries.name: Sand Dunes Chaolao Beach Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Chao Lao Beach · beachfront · large 185-room resort

rooms.type: Deluxe Corner Sea View (46 sq m)

entries.addr: 73 Moo 5, Chaloem Burapha Chonlathit Road, Khlong Khut subdistrict, Tha Mai
entries.storyHtml: If the reviews had to pick the biggest, most complete family resort on Chao Lao Beach, the name that comes up most is Sand Dunes Chaolao Beach Resort — a large 4-star beachfront resort with 185 rooms, scoring about 9.0 from over 230 reviews, the highest score in this article. What makes plenty of parents choose it is that it's genuinely designed for families — a big pool, lots of kids' activities, wide communal areas, and a Family Room that comfortably sleeps 3, so bringing the kids and the grandparents along never feels cramped. The entry-level Superior Twin at 31 sq m is also roomier than a lot of places in the same area, and anyone after a straight sea view can step up to the Deluxe Corner Sea View with a wide balcony looking right out to the water. Reviews are fairly consistent in praising the service and cleanliness — staff who look after you well, a beachfront spot you can walk straight into the sea from, and safe space for kids to run around. Honest caveats: like every stay in this area, the sea on the Chao Lao side isn't as clear as the south's, and the public beach beyond the resort has litter in places during the monsoon season. It's a big resort, so on long weekends it gets busy and the pool gets crowded — anyone who likes quiet and privacy may find it lively. In short, if the goal is bringing the family to splash around on Chao Lao Beach on a manageable budget, Sand Dunes is the safest pick and the best-scoring one in this set.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: if you're coming as a group or with kids, pick the Family Room — it's better value than booking two rooms. If you want a real sea view, specify the Deluxe Corner Sea View, and avoid long weekends unless you don't mind a crowded pool and lots of people.
pros: Large beachfront resort, 9.0 — the highest score in the article
Designed for families — big pool, lots of kids' activities, wide spaces
Entry rooms at 31 sq m, roomier than many places in the same area
Consistent service and cleanliness, staff who look after you well (from reviews)
cons: The Chao Lao sea isn't as clear as the south's
The public beach beyond the resort has litter in places by season
Big resort — busy and crowded pool on long weekends (from reviews)

entries.type: 4-Star Resort · On Chao Lao Beach · Pool Access available
entries.name: Chaolao Cabana Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Chao Lao Beach · beachfront · Pool Access rooms
entries.addr: 18/1 Moo 5, Chaloem Burapha Chonlathit Road, Khlong Khut subdistrict, Chao Lao Beach, Tha Mai
entries.storyHtml: Chaolao Cabana Resort is a neighbour not far from Tosang on the same Chao Lao Beach strip, but it sells a slightly different angle — a 4-star resort of around 50 rooms and villas, scoring about 8.6 from over 287 reviews, where a lot of people come for the sea-view infinity pool and the Pool Access rooms you can step straight into the pool from your balcony. That's the thing reviews mention most, because it gives the feel of a pricier resort at a price that's still reachable — Deluxe rooms start around ฿1,900, while Deluxe Pool Access sits around ฿4,000. Groups or families can also pick a Cabana Villa of around 56 sq m. The spot is on Chao Lao Beach, walkable into the sea just the same, and most reviews praise the leafy, shaded setting and the easygoing staff. Breakfast is fine for the price. Honest caveats from the reviews: it isn't a five-star resort — rooms in the older block have little details to pick at on age and upkeep — and, like the whole area, the Chao Lao sea isn't clear and the beach has litter in places by season. Some reviews say the pool feels a touch small when it's busy on holidays, and parking is limited when the resort is full. The thing to understand is that it's a mid-size resort without the lively kids' activities of Sand Dunes — it leans more toward a quiet, restful stay. In short, if you want the pool-villa feel or a sea-view infinity pool on Chao Lao Beach on a budget that isn't steep, and you're happy with a low-key stay, Chaolao Cabana is one of the best-value, best-atmosphere picks on this strip.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: if you want the full resort feel, pick the Deluxe Pool Access you can step into the pool from your balcony. For groups of friends or larger families, the Cabana Villa is better value. Book ahead on long weekends, because the Pool Access rooms are limited and fill fast.

entries.type: 3-Star Riverside Beach Resort · River Mouth–Chao Lao Beach
entries.name: Blues River Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 River mouth–Chao Lao Beach · near Kung Krabaen

rooms.type: Blue Pool View (near the waterslide pool)

entries.addr: 1/8-9 Moo 4, Khlong Khut subdistrict, Tha Mai
entries.storyHtml: Blues River Resort breaks from the straight-up beachfront stays, because it sits right at the mouth of a river that flows out to meet Chao Lao Beach — riverside and seaside atmosphere in one place. It's a 3-star, 56-room resort that opened in 2019, scoring about 8.8 from over 42 reviews. What kids love most, and reviews mention often, is the pool with a waterslide, which makes it a family stay where the children can splash happily all day, plus there's a private beach and it's close to the Kung Krabaen Bay nature study centre, the area's regular day trip. The entry-level Standard is very light at around ฿1,400 but has no balcony, so anyone after some atmosphere can step up to a Garden View or a Riverside room, some of which have a balcony and a private garden. Reviews praise the quiet setting, the value, and the privacy of the beach. The honest caveat to know: it's a fairly new resort and the review scores swing clearly from one period to another — some older reviews fault the room cleanliness and an inconsistent breakfast, while newer ones are better, which means quality depends on when you go and how it's being run. In short, it suits families and couples driving to Chanthaburi who want a waterslide pool and quiet riverside-meets-beach atmosphere in the low-thousand-baht range — but read the latest reviews before booking.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: skip the Standard if you want a balcony — step up to a Garden View or Riverside instead. Read the latest reviews from the past 2–3 months before booking, since quality swings by period. If you're bringing kids, the waterslide pool is the highlight, so leave plenty of pool time.

entries.type: Seaside Resort · On Chao Lao Beach · Leafy garden
entries.name: Baan Imm Sook Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Chao Lao Beach · near the beach, private beach
entries.addr: 50/7 Moo 5, Khlong Khut subdistrict, Tha Mai
entries.storyHtml: Baan Imm Sook Resort is the name people chasing quiet tend to land on — a seaside resort of around 47 rooms on Chao Lao Beach, scoring as high as about 9.0 from over 44 reviews, and nearly every review talks about the leafy garden setting, the cleanliness, and the quiet privacy rather than any sell on luxury. It suits a slow, restful trip — there's a private beach, a pool, a playground, free bikes to borrow, and, as many agree, a breakfast that's tastier than you'd expect for a stay this size. The entry-level Deluxe Garden starts around ฿1,600 and suits couples, while families have a Family Room for 4 and a Suite with a separate living area for longer stays. The staff draw consistent praise — reviews call them warm and attentive, like staying at a relative's house. Honest caveats from the reviews: most rooms have a garden view, not a full sea view, so if you expect to open the curtains to the sea you may be disappointed; the resort is near the beach but you have to walk out a little — not every room is right on the sand. It's a small stay focused on calm — it doesn't have the full facilities of a big resort or any lively activities. In short, if you want a clean, quiet, leafy Chao Lao Beach stay for a slow-life family trip at a good price, Baan Imm Sook delivers, and the high score backs it up.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: set your expectation to a leafy garden view, not a full sea view, and you won't be disappointed. Borrow the free bikes for a ride along the beach morning and evening. If you're a bigger group, pick the Family Room or the Suite — better value, with a living area.
pros: High score around 9.0 — leafy garden setting, clean and quiet
Private beach, pool, playground, free bikes
Breakfast tastier than expected, warm and attentive staff (from reviews)

cons: Most rooms have a garden view, not a full sea view

entries.type: 4-Star Hotel · Near Chao Lao Beach · Pool villa available
entries.name: Villa Blanca Hotel & Restaurant
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Chao Lao Beach · near the beach (cross the road)

rooms.type: Queen Deluxe (~25 sq m · garden/pool view)

entries.addr: 72/1 Moo 5, Chaloem Burapha Chonlathit Road, Khlong Khut subdistrict, Tha Mai
entries.storyHtml: Villa Blanca Hotel & Restaurant sells a different look from its neighbours in this area — it's a white Mediterranean-style building that photographs beautifully, a 4-star hotel of around 43–50 rooms and villas, scoring about 8.4 from over 493 reviews, one of the highest review counts in the article. What reviews mention often is the two saltwater pools that don't sting the eyes, good for kids, and the two-bedroom pool villa with a private pool and a barbecue area for groups or larger families. The standard Queen Deluxe starts around ฿1,500, very easy to reach, and there's an on-site restaurant that's handy when you don't feel like going out. Staff draw praise for being friendly, and room cleanliness sits in the good range. The most important honest caveat: the hotel isn't right on the beach — you have to walk across a road to reach it, unlike Tosang or Sand Dunes that are on the sand, so anyone expecting to open the door to the sea should understand that first. On top of that, the building has no lift, so upper-floor rooms mean stairs, and the in-room facilities are fairly basic for the price — some reviews say most room views are of the garden or the pool, not the sea. Another thing to allow for: long weekends get busy and the pool can crowd, so book rooms and the pool villa ahead because the villas are limited. In short, it suits people who want a clean seaside Chanthaburi stay with a photogenic building, saltwater pools for the kids, or a private pool villa on a reachable budget — and who aren't fussed about opening the door straight onto the sand.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: understand before booking that you cross a road to the beach — it isn't on the sand. For a group or larger family, the Pool Villa is good value and comes with a private pool. If stairs are hard for you, ask for a ground-floor room, since the building has no lift.

Two saltwater pools that don't sting the eyes, good for kids
A two-bedroom Pool Villa with a private pool and a barbecue area
Easy starting price of ฿1,500, with an on-site restaurant (from reviews)
cons: Not right on the beach — you walk across a road to reach it

entries.type: Small Seaside Resort · On Chao Lao Beach · Pet-friendly
entries.name: Baan Sood Kob Fah
entries.badge: 🐶 Bring your dog or cat · beachfront
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Chao Lao Beach · beachfront, walk straight into the sea
entries.addr: 3/2 Moo 6, Khlong Khut subdistrict, Chao Lao Beach, Tha Mai
entries.storyHtml: Baan Sood Kob Fah ("House at the Edge of the Sky") is a small stay on Chao Lao Beach with a different kind of charm from the big resorts in this article — a house-and-bungalow-style beachfront stay you can walk straight into the sea from, scoring about 8.4 from around 60 real reviews, and the selling point a certain crowd loves is that you can bring your dog or cat, which is hard to find at a seaside stay. The feel here is quiet and private, without the bustle of a big resort — there's a seaside barbecue corner to sit, catch the breeze and watch the view in the evening, and a very light starting price of around ฿1,000 for an air-conditioned double room with a TV, fridge and en-suite bathroom. The seaside houses and the large house for families or groups of friends are priced on request, by size and season. Reviews praise the genuinely beachfront spot, the privacy, and the friendly owner. The honest caveat to know: it's a small stay with no pool and not the full service of a big resort — the rooms and houses are simple rather than luxurious, and most of it has to be booked directly with the property rather than across every online platform, so the links here are search pages — call or message the page to confirm rooms and prices first. In short, it suits people who prize the sea and the calm, are bringing a pet, and are happy to trade simplicity for the cheapest price in the article.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: book directly with the property (phone/page) to confirm rooms, prices and the pet policy, since it isn't on every platform. Set your expectation to a simple house focused on the sea and the calm — no pool and none of the big-resort service.

entries.type: 4-Star Beachfront Resort · On Laem Sadet–Chao Lao Beach
entries.name: Saint Tropez Beach Resort
entries.badge: 🏡 Beachfront villas · easy on the budget

rooms.type: Beach Front Villa (~75 sq m · 2 storeys)

entries.addr: 54/6 Moo 4, Laem Sadet Beach, Khlong Khut subdistrict, Tha Mai
entries.storyHtml: Saint Tropez Beach Resort sits on Laem Sadet Beach, which runs on from Chao Lao Beach. It's an 89-room, 4-star beachfront resort scoring about 8.0 from over 44 reviews, leaning on a beachfront spot and a reachable price rather than polish. What reviews mention is the pool, a spot you can walk down to the beach from, and — the interesting part — a Beach Front Villa, a private two-storey house on the beach of around 75 sq m, of which there are only a few, suited to groups or families who want privacy on the sand, from around ฿4,500, which is good value for a beachfront villa. Rooms in the main building start at just around ฿1,500, making it a budget-friendly option, and the Executive Suite at around 64 sq m is wide enough for a family. The honest caveat to know before booking: it scores lower than many in the article because the room quality and service are still up and down — reviews include people praising the spot and people faulting the upkeep. There's feedback about noise on nights with tour groups or large parties staying, and a breakfast that many say could still improve. Like the whole area, the sea on this side isn't as clear as island water. In short, it suits people focused on sleeping by the beach on a modest budget — especially groups after a value beachfront villa — who can live with rooms and service that aren't consistent on every point. Read the latest reviews alongside.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: if you're a group, the Beach Front Villa is good value and gives you privacy on the sand. If you're sensitive to noise, avoid times with big groups and ask for a room away from the communal areas. Read the latest reviews and compare prices across 3 sites before booking, since quality still varies.

entries.type: Seaside Resort · On Laem Sadet/Chao Lao Beach · Tropical style
entries.name: Maldives Beach Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Laem Sadet/Chao Lao Beach · beachfront, on-site café
entries.addr: 33/2 Moo 4, Laem Sadet Beach, Khlong Khut subdistrict, Tha Mai
entries.storyHtml: Maldives Beach Resort plays on its image clearly, right from the name — a white tropical mood that photographs beautifully and looks crisp and clean, set on Laem Sadet Beach where it runs on from Chao Lao. It's a seaside resort of around 40–70 rooms and villas, scoring about 8.3 from over 400 reviews, one of the highest review counts in the article. What draws people is the private beach, the sea-view rooms, and an on-site café and seaside seafood restaurant that let you sit, relax, take photos and catch the sea breeze without going anywhere. The entry-level Standard/Superior starts around ฿1,800 with breakfast included, good for couples on a budget, while anyone after a full sea view has the Panoramic Seaview Suite on floors 2–3 that opens the curtains to the sea, and the Beachfront/Pool Villa you can walk from your room onto the sand. Reviews praise the atmosphere, the photogenic looks, the quiet beach, and the seaside food. Honest caveats from the reviews: the resort is still being developed and steadily upgraded, with notes about construction/renovation in places, cleanliness that's uneven in spots, and a spot where the shops and convenience stores are far away — you have to drive out. Prices for the sea-view rooms and villas climb fairly high compared with the neighbours. In short, it suits couples and photo lovers who want a pretty, quiet seaside resort within a day's drive of Bangkok — but set your expectations on polish accordingly and read the latest reviews before booking.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: for a full sea view, pick the Panoramic Seaview Suite or the Beachfront Villa outright, since the entry rooms face inward. Bring your own food and supplies, because the convenience stores are far. Read the latest reviews to check whether there's renovation work during your dates.

Private beach, sea-view rooms, and an on-site café + seaside seafood
Entry rooms from ฿1,800 with breakfast, plus a Pool Villa on the beach
Quiet atmosphere, good for couples and photo lovers (from reviews)

entries.type: 3-Star Beach Resort · On Seashell/Chao Lao Beach
entries.name: Seashell Village Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Seashell/Chao Lao Beach · fairly far, car needed
entries.addr: 50 Moo 6, Khlong Khut subdistrict, Tha Mai (Seashell/Chao Lao Beach)
entries.storyHtml: Seashell Village Resort closes the article with a pick for people who want to escape the bustle and sleep by the sea at a genuinely slow pace — a small 3-star beach resort of around 29 rooms on Seashell Beach, which runs on from Chao Lao, scoring about 7.6 from over 264 reviews. What reviews agree on is a private, uncrowded beach and a pool with a wide, roughly 180-degree sea view, plus water activities, which make it a stay with real quiet and a lot of privacy — good for couples or anyone after a break without the crowds. Standard rooms start around ฿1,950, and there's a Sea View Sea Suite with a jacuzzi, up to a Pool Access room with a private pool for anyone after the most privacy. The honest caveat behind the lowest score in the article: the spot is fairly far and hard to reach without a car — restaurants and convenience stores around it are limited, and you have to drive a good way out. It's a resort that's been open a while, so there's wear with age and some upkeep details reviews fault, such as room cleanliness and small inconsistencies, which leaves the overall score around 7.6, below the others in the article. Another thing to know is that the food and dining options at the resort are limited, and with the outside shops being far, bringing your own food is easier. In short, it suits only people with their own car who prize quiet and privacy and a sea view from the pool above all, and who can live with simplicity and a spot far from the shops in exchange for an uncrowded, quiet beach and the feeling of a real rest.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: you'll need your own car, and bring your own food and supplies, because the surrounding shops are limited. For the full feel, pick a sea-view room or Pool Access. Read the latest reviews on room upkeep before booking, since the overall score is below the others in the article.

Good for couples and anyone after a slow-life break (from reviews)

noteHtml: 📌 Note: all prices are approximate starting prices from the standard-room range and may change by date and season — always check the real price and compare 3 sites before booking. The scores and highlights in this article come from reading guests' real reviews on the booking platforms; we did not stay ourselves. The sea on the Chao Lao–Laem Sadet side is sand mixed with mud and not as clear as island water, and the public beach has litter in places during the monsoon season (May–October), so check conditions during your trip. Baan Sood Kob Fah mostly has to be booked directly with the property. On long weekends and in high season (November–February) prices rise and rooms fill fast, so book ahead. Chao Lao Beach is in Tha Mai district, about 25–30 min from Chanthaburi town — having your own car is by far the easiest. Article by ThailandAddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — questions travellers ask most about Chao Lao Beach stays in Chanthaburi

faq.q: ❓ Which is the best Chao Lao Beach stay in Chanthaburi?
faq.a: It depends on your trip style. For a family splash-around with a full resort, Sand Dunes Chaolao Beach Resort has the highest score in the article at 9.0 — beachfront, with a big pool and lots of kids' activities. For the most reviews and best value, Chaolao Tosang Beach Hotel has the most, over 1,145. For quiet and clean, Baan Imm Sook Resort scores 9.0. For an infinity pool and Pool Access, Chaolao Cabana Resort. And for a tight budget sleeping by the beach, Baan Sood Kob Fah starts at just ฿1,000.

faq.q: ❓ How much do Chao Lao Beach stays cost?
faq.a: In this article, prices start at about ฿1,000–4,500 per night for standard up to sea-view rooms. The cheapest are Baan Sood Kob Fah from ฿1,000 and Blues River from ฿1,400. Most sit in the ฿1,500–2,200 range. Sea-view rooms, villas and Pool Villas can climb to ฿4,500–8,500 by size and season. Prices on long weekends and in high season are higher than usual, so book ahead.

faq.q: ❓ How do you get to Chao Lao Beach — do you need a car?
faq.a: Chao Lao Beach is in Tha Mai district, Chanthaburi, about 25–30 min from Chanthaburi town and roughly 3.5–4 hours from Bangkok via the motorway. Having your own car or a rental is by far the easiest, because there's no public transport that runs all the way to the beach — the stays are spread along the coast and sights like Kung Krabaen Bay need a car. If you take a coach to the town, you'll need a connecting ride.

faq.q: ❓ Is the sea at Chao Lao Beach nice — is the water clear?
faq.a: You should understand honestly that Chao Lao–Laem Sadet is a sand-mixed-with-mud beach, not as clear as the islands or the south — it's better for resting, strolling the shore and catching the breeze than for snorkelling over coral. During the monsoon (May–October) the public beach has litter in places and the water is murkier than usual. The appeal here is the closeness to Bangkok, the affordable stays and the calm — more than clear sea water.

faq.q: ❓ Which Chao Lao Beach stay is good for kids and families?
faq.a: The most family-focused is Sand Dunes Chaolao Beach Resort — a large beachfront resort with a big pool, lots of kids' activities and a Family Room. Next is Blues River Resort with a waterslide pool the kids love. Chaolao Tosang and Villa Blanca also have a separate kids' pool / saltwater pools for the children. Every one is on or near the beach so you can take the little ones onto the sand.

faq.q: ❓ Is there a pet-friendly Chao Lao Beach stay?
faq.a: Yes. Baan Sood Kob Fah ("House at the Edge of the Sky") is a small stay on Chao Lao Beach that's dog- and cat-friendly, which is hard to find at a seaside stay — from just around ฿1,000, beachfront and walk straight into the sea, with a seaside barbecue corner. It's a small stay that mostly has to be booked directly, so call or message the page to confirm the pet policy and price before booking.
